note: Catalog of agentic design-pattern families and architectures used by setup_agent.py to scaffold an agent's _execute. Pattern names are the field-standard names; descriptions, when_to_use, steps and topology are our own wording and structural interpretation. `reference` links to public material for further reading; no third-party source code or prose is reproduced. Families follow the common literature (Reflection, Planning, Tool Use, Multi-Agent; plus Retrieval, Memory, Routing), with Sampling & Search and Specialty.

topologies.loop: The last step cycles back to the first until the result is good enough.
topologies.cycle: Tight back-edge between the last two steps (e.g. think / act / observe).
topologies.parallel: Fan out to N independent runs, then aggregate.
topologies.tree: A coordinator fans out to the middle steps, then converges.

families.name: Reflection & Refinement
families.description: The agent drafts, critiques its own output, and revises in a loop — improving a single answer by self-review, with no external systems involved.
families.when_to_use: A first draft is often flawed and self-critique reliably improves it.
families.needs: Just an LLM — no tools or external data.
families.cost: Medium: several LLM calls (one per critique/revise round).

families.name: Retrieval
families.description: The agent grounds its answer in evidence pulled from an external, read-only corpus or index at query time, rather than relying on parametric memory.
families.when_to_use: Answers must be grounded in a corpus or cite sources, not model memory.
families.needs: An external read-only document store or index to pull from.
families.cost: Low–medium: retrieval + 1–2 LLM calls; corrective variants add passes.

families.name: Planning & Chaining
families.description: The agent decomposes a goal into an ordered sequence of sub-steps, executes them, and replans on failure — optionally searching over plans.
families.when_to_use: A goal is big enough to decompose into ordered steps, with replanning.
families.needs: Usually tools to run steps; optionally a search budget (ToT/LATS).
families.cost: Medium–high: planning + per-step execution; search multiplies calls.

families.name: Tool Use & Actions
families.description: The agent acts on the world by calling out to an external tool, API, or MCP server, then incorporates the observation — reasoning interleaved with action.
families.when_to_use: The task needs an external action: call an API, run code, drive a tool.
families.needs: One or more tools / an MCP server the agent calls out to.
families.cost: Low–medium: a few LLM calls; cost scales with tool round-trips.

families.name: Memory
families.description: The agent reads from and writes to a persistent store that survives across turns and sessions, accumulating experience it can reuse later.
families.when_to_use: Long-running / repeat use where the agent should learn across sessions.
families.needs: A persistent read-write store (vector/graph/DB) spanning turns.
families.cost: Medium: recall + write each turn; store grows over time.

families.name: Routing & Governance
families.description: The agent gates or routes work with a deterministic (non-LLM) decision — approving, blocking, escalating to a human, or dispatching to the right path.
families.when_to_use: Actions carry risk/cost, or requests must route to the right path.
families.needs: A deterministic check/policy (gate), optionally human approval.
families.cost: Low: the gate is a cheap Python branch; safety over extra LLM spend.

families.name: Sampling & Search
families.description: The agent draws many samples from a space — LLM reasoning paths OR a numerical/parameter space — evaluates each, and aggregates: vote for the best (self-consistency, ensemble) or keep the whole distribution (Monte Carlo forward uncertainty quantification, simulator ensembles). Fan out, then aggregate.
families.when_to_use: You must explore many samples and aggregate — pick the best answer, or quantify a distribution (forward UQ / Monte Carlo over a model).
families.needs: An LLM and/or an external model/simulator to evaluate per sample; optionally a scorer to rank.
families.cost: High: N samples means N× the per-sample cost (LLM calls or simulator runs).

families.name: Multi-Agent
families.description: Multiple specialized agents coordinate — a supervisor routing to specialists, a shared workspace, debate, or multi-perspective research — then converge.
families.when_to_use: Work splits into distinct roles/perspectives better handled separately.
families.needs: Multiple agents (often A2A), each possibly with its own tools.
families.cost: High: many agents × their own calls; coordination overhead.

families.name: Specialty
families.description: Patterns with an unusual shape that no standard family fits — written constitutions, learned self-improvement over an archive, rule-driven cellular dynamics.
families.when_to_use: Unusual structure no standard family fits (constitutions, CA, self-evolve).
families.needs: Varies by pattern — stated per architecture.
families.cost: Varies — outliers; check the specific architecture.

architectures.name: Reflection
architectures.description: Draft an answer, critique it against the goal, then revise. A generate-critique-revise loop that improves a single answer.
architectures.when_to_use: A first draft is usually close but flawed, and a self-critique pass reliably improves it.
steps: Produce an initial answer to the task.
Critique the draft against the goal; list concrete flaws.
Revise the draft using the critique. Loop if not good enough.

architectures.name: Reflexion
architectures.description: Reflection plus verbal self-feedback stored across attempts: the agent writes lessons from a failed try and conditions the next try on them.
architectures.when_to_use: Multi-attempt tasks with a success signal, where remembering why the last attempt failed helps the next.
steps: Check the attempt against a success signal.
If failed, write a short lesson; store it for the next try.

architectures.name: Chain of Verification
architectures.description: Produce an answer, generate independent verification questions, answer those, and reconcile — catching unsupported claims.
architectures.when_to_use: Factual answers where hallucinated details must be caught before returning.
steps: Revise the answer to drop unsupported claims.

architectures.name: Self-Discover
architectures.description: The agent selects and composes reasoning modules into a task-specific plan before solving, rather than using a fixed prompt structure.
architectures.when_to_use: Diverse problem types where the best reasoning structure differs per task.
steps: Select reasoning modules relevant to the task.
Compose the selected modules into a task plan.
Execute the composed plan to solve the task.

architectures.name: Mental Loop
architectures.description: The agent simulates outcomes of candidate actions in an internal model before committing, a lightweight look-ahead.
architectures.when_to_use: Decisions where cheaply imagining consequences avoids an expensive wrong action.
steps: Simulate each action's likely outcome internally.
Commit to the action with the best simulated outcome.

architectures.name: Self-Consistency
architectures.description: Sample several independent reasoning paths and take the majority/consensus answer.
architectures.when_to_use: Short-answer problems where independent samples agree more often than any single path is right.
steps: Sample N independent reasoning paths for the task.
Take the majority / consensus answer across samples.

architectures.name: Forward Sampling / Monte Carlo UQ
architectures.description: Draw samples from input distributions, run a forward model or simulator once per sample, and aggregate the output distribution — mean, variance, confidence intervals. Keeps the whole distribution rather than voting a single best answer.
architectures.when_to_use: Propagating input uncertainty through a model or simulator: forward UQ, Monte Carlo, parameter sweeps, simulator ensembles. Pair with Tool Use to call the simulator per sample.
steps: Define input parameter distributions to sample.
Draw N samples from the input space.
Run the forward model/simulator once per sample (a tool call).
Aggregate the output distribution: mean, variance, intervals.

architectures.name: Tree of Thoughts
architectures.description: Search a tree of partial reasoning states with explicit expand/evaluate/backtrack, rather than a single chain.
architectures.when_to_use: Puzzles or planning where dead ends are common and backtracking pays off.
steps: Expand candidate next thoughts from the current state.
Select/backtrack; repeat until a solution state is reached.

architectures.name: LATS
architectures.description: Language Agent Tree Search: Monte-Carlo-style search over actions with reflection and value estimates guiding expansion.
architectures.when_to_use: Tool-using tasks with a scorable outcome where guided search beats greedy acting.
steps: Expand candidate actions from the current node.
Roll out / estimate value for candidates.
Reflect on failures to guide the next expansion.

architectures.name: Ensemble
architectures.description: Run several distinct agents/prompts and aggregate their outputs (vote, merge, or pick) for robustness.
architectures.when_to_use: You can afford multiple runs and want variance reduction or coverage across approaches.
steps: Run several distinct agents/prompts on the task.
Vote, merge, or pick across member outputs.

architectures.name: Agentic RAG
architectures.description: The agent decides when and what to retrieve, issuing its own queries as part of reasoning rather than retrieving once up front.
architectures.when_to_use: Questions needing multiple or iterative lookups the agent must plan itself.
steps: Decide what to retrieve for this question.
Answer grounded in the retrieved evidence.

architectures.name: Corrective RAG
architectures.description: Grade retrieved documents for relevance; when they are weak, correct course (re-query or fall back to web/other sources) before answering.
architectures.when_to_use: Retrieval quality is uneven and answering on bad context must be avoided.
steps: If weak, re-query or fall back to another source.
Answer grounded only in sufficiently-relevant evidence.

architectures.name: Self-RAG
architectures.description: The model emits reflection tokens deciding whether to retrieve, and critiques its own grounding and support as it generates.
architectures.when_to_use: Answers must self-assess whether each claim is actually supported by retrieved text.
steps: Decide whether retrieval is needed for this span.
Keep only claims the retrieved text supports.

architectures.name: Adaptive RAG
architectures.description: Route each query to the cheapest sufficient strategy — no retrieval, single-shot, or iterative — based on estimated difficulty.
architectures.when_to_use: A mix of easy and hard queries where always-iterating wastes cost and never-iterating fails hard ones.
steps: Estimate difficulty; route to no/single/iterative retrieval.

architectures.name: GraphRAG
architectures.description: Retrieve over a knowledge graph (entities + relationships), enabling multi-hop and global-summary questions a flat index cannot answer.
architectures.when_to_use: Corpora with rich entity relationships and questions that span many documents.
steps: Traverse the knowledge graph for multi-hop context.

architectures.name: Episodic + Semantic Memory
architectures.description: Separate stores for specific past episodes and distilled general facts, retrieved to inform new responses.
architectures.when_to_use: Assistants that should recall both what happened before and what they have learned in general.
steps: Retrieve relevant past episodes and semantic facts.
Respond using recalled memory + the current input.

architectures.name: Graph Memory
architectures.description: Persist memory as a typed knowledge graph so relationships between remembered items are first-class and queryable.
architectures.when_to_use: Memory where connections between facts matter as much as the facts themselves.
steps: Query the memory graph for related nodes.
Insert new nodes/edges from this interaction.

architectures.name: MemGPT
architectures.description: Treat the context window like RAM with an OS-style memory manager paging information in and out of a larger store.
architectures.when_to_use: Conversations or documents far larger than the context window.
steps: Page relevant context in from the external store.
Respond using the active context window.
Summarize/evict and persist to the external store.

architectures.name: Voyager
architectures.description: Build a growing library of reusable skills from experience, composing learned skills to tackle harder tasks over time.
architectures.when_to_use: Open-ended environments where the agent should get more capable the longer it runs.
steps: Pick or compose skills from the library for the task.
Distill a reusable skill from success; store it.

architectures.name: Agent Workflow Memory
architectures.description: Induce reusable workflows from past successful trajectories and reuse them to shortcut future similar tasks.
architectures.when_to_use: Repetitive task families where remembering a known-good procedure saves rediscovery.
steps: Match the task to an induced reusable workflow.
Execute the matched workflow (or solve from scratch).
Induce a new workflow from a successful trajectory.

architectures.name: Tool Use
architectures.description: The simplest acting pattern: the model calls a single external tool and incorporates the result.
architectures.when_to_use: One capability the model lacks (search, calculation, a single API) is enough.
steps: Decide which tool to call and with what arguments.
Call the tool. TODO(author): implement the tool.
Incorporate the tool result into the answer.

architectures.name: ReAct
architectures.description: Interleave Thought, Action, and Observation so reasoning guides each tool call and observations guide the next thought.
architectures.when_to_use: Multi-step tasks needing several tool calls whose results shape subsequent reasoning.
steps: Reason about what to do next (Thought).
Take an action / call a tool (Action).
Record the result (Observation). Loop until done.

architectures.name: Planning
architectures.description: Decompose the goal into an explicit plan, execute steps, and replan when steps fail.
architectures.when_to_use: Tasks long enough that an up-front plan reduces thrashing, with replanning for surprises.
steps: Decompose the goal into an explicit ordered plan.
Replan when a step fails or reality diverges.

architectures.name: Plan-Execute-Verify
architectures.description: Plan, execute each step, and verify its result before proceeding — accepting, retrying, or escalating per step.
architectures.when_to_use: Pipelines where a silently wrong intermediate step would corrupt the final result.
steps: Verify the step result; accept, retry, or escalate.

architectures.name: SWE-Agent
architectures.description: A sandboxed file-system/coding agent with read/write/run tools that edits a repo and checks its own work.
architectures.when_to_use: Software tasks that require navigating and modifying a codebase and running checks.
steps: Read relevant files in the sandbox.
Write changes. TODO(author): wire sandboxed fs tools.

architectures.name: Browser / Computer Use
architectures.description: Drive a real browser or computer with categorical actions, gated by a deterministic safety check.
architectures.when_to_use: Tasks that only a GUI exposes, where unsafe actions must be blocked by a non-LLM gate.
steps: Deterministic safety check — block unsafe actions.
Execute the action if the gate passed.
Observe the new state; loop until done.

architectures.name: Multi-Agent (Supervisor + Specialists)
architectures.description: A supervisor decomposes the task and routes sub-tasks to specialist agents, then synthesizes their outputs.
architectures.when_to_use: Work that cleanly splits into distinct expertises coordinated by a lead.
steps: Supervisor splits the task into sub-tasks.
Route each sub-task to a specialist. TODO(author): specialists.
Combine specialist outputs into the final answer.

architectures.name: Blackboard
architectures.description: Specialists read from and write to a shared workspace, contributing opportunistically until the solution converges.
architectures.when_to_use: Loosely-ordered collaboration where any specialist may contribute whenever it can help.
steps: Write the problem to the shared workspace.
Stop when the workspace holds a complete solution.

architectures.name: Debate
architectures.description: N agents argue a question over K rounds; a judge or deterministic rule resolves the stronger position.
architectures.when_to_use: Contested questions where surfacing counter-arguments improves the decision — but watch for group-think.
steps: Run K rounds of rebuttal between N agents.
Resolve the stronger position (deterministic rule or judge).

architectures.name: STORM
architectures.description: Simulate multiple perspectives asking questions, gather grounded answers, and synthesize a structured article.
architectures.when_to_use: Producing a comprehensive, multi-perspective report or survey from research.
steps: Generate multiple perspectives that ask questions.
Answer each question with grounded evidence.
Synthesize a structured article from the answers.

architectures.name: Meta-Controller
architectures.description: A router that selects among whole architectures/agents per request, dispatching each task to the best-suited one.
architectures.when_to_use: A heterogeneous workload where different requests are best served by different patterns.
steps: Classify the request and select the best sub-architecture.
Dispatch to the chosen sub-agent. TODO(author): sub-agents.

architectures.name: Dry-Run
architectures.description: Propose an action, simulate it, and require approval (automatic, reviewer, or blocked) before any real effect.
architectures.when_to_use: Actions with real-world consequences that must be previewed and gated before execution.
steps: Approve automatically, send to a reviewer, or block.

architectures.name: Reflexive Metacognitive Routing
architectures.description: The agent assesses its own capability for a task and routes to a stronger path or human when confidence is low — the override being a deterministic check.
architectures.when_to_use: Mixed-difficulty tasks where the agent should know its limits and escalate rather than guess.
steps: Assess own capability/confidence for this task.
Deterministic check: escalate to a stronger path or human if low.

architectures.name: Constitutional AI
architectures.description: The agent critiques and revises its own outputs against an explicit written set of principles (a constitution).
architectures.when_to_use: Outputs must conform to stated policies or values and self-governance is preferred to a separate filter.
steps: Critique it against the written principles.
Revise to comply with the constitution.

architectures.name: RLHF Self-Improvement
architectures.description: Score candidates on multiple deterministic dimensions, keep the best in an archive, and improve against that composite signal over time.
architectures.when_to_use: There is a measurable multi-dimensional quality signal and you want the agent to improve across runs.
steps: Keep the best in an archive; improve against the composite.

architectures.name: Cellular Automata
architectures.description: Apply LLM-expressed local rules repeatedly over a grid of cells to produce emergent global behavior.
architectures.when_to_use: Modeling spatial or emergent dynamics from simple local rules.
steps: Apply local LLM-expressed rules to every cell.
Advance the grid; repeat for N steps.

frameworks.base_entrypoint: StateGraph nodes + edges, compiled and invoked

frameworks.base_entrypoint: Agent(...) with a typed result model, run_sync
